'''Dietrich Belitz''' (born 1955) is an American [[List of theoretical physicists|theoretical physicist]] on the faculty of the [[University of Oregon]]. He studies [[statistical mechanics]] and [[Condensed matter physics|condensed matter]]  physics.

== Early life and education ==
Belitz earned his Diploma in 1980 and his [[Dr. rer. nat.]] degree in 1982, both from the [[Technical University of Munich]] (Germany). His dissertation was titled, ''Der Einfluß inkohärenter Tunnelprozesse auf die Leitfähigkeit ungeordneter Materialien (trans.: The influence of incoherent tunneling processes on the conductivity of disordered materials),'' advised by [[Wolfgang Götze]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE |url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/1016888 |access-date=2022-04-02 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Physics Tree - Dietrich Belitz |url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=448954 |access-date=2022-04-17 |website=academictree.org}}</ref> He did postdoctoral work at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2021-01-04 |title=Meet Our New RMP Colloquia Editor |url=https://journals.aps.org/rmp/edannounce/new-rmp-colloquia-editor |access-date=2022-04-02 |website=Reviews of Modern Physics |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dietrich Belitz {{!}} Institute for Fundamental Science |url=https://ifs.uoregon.edu/profile/dbelitz/ |access-date=2022-04-02 |website=ifs.uoregon.edu}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 1987 Belitz joined the faculty at the University of Oregon and is a member of the  Materials Science Institute there.<ref name=":0" /> Belitz became a professor of physics in 1997.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Belitz |first=Dietrich |date=2020 |title=Curriculum vitae |url=https://pages.uoregon.edu/dbelitz/db_virtual/pdf/cv.pdf |access-date=April 1, 2022 |website=University of Oregon}}</ref> His research has included [[statistical mechanics]], [[Condensed matter physics|condensed matter]], and theory of quantum [[Many-body problem|many-body systems]]."<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 2004 |title=CAS News, Introducing Dietrich Belitz |url=https://scholarsbank.uoregon.edu/xmlui/bitstream/handle/1794/4283/cascade_2004autumn.pdf?sequence=1 |access-date=April 2, 2022 |website=scholarsbank.uoregon.edu/}}</ref>

''[[Reviews of Modern Physics]]'' describes Belitz' interests as, "...&nbsp;focused on quantum many-body problems, including [[superconductivity]], [[magnetism]], [[Transport phenomena|transport processes]], and [[Quantum phase transition|quantum phase transitions]]."<ref name=":0" />

Belitz is a member of the University's Condensed Matter Theory & Statistical Mechanics group,<ref name=":1" /> which describes their work as the study of:{{Blockquote|text=... strongly fluctuating systems with a large number (e.g., the [[Avogadro number]]!) of degrees of freedom. These include quantum many-body problems, "soft" phases of matter, and biological systems. The quantum phenomena we study include superconductivity and magnetism; quantum phase transitions, in particular [[Metal–insulator transition|metal-insulator]] and magnetic transitions; and [[Transport theory (statistical physics)|transport theory]]. The soft systems include [[liquid crystals]]; complex fluids; slender flexible structures (e.g. [[polymer chains]], a sheet of paper, or a ping-pong ball); [[Macromolecule|macromolecular]] liquids and mixtures, and their phase separation through coarse-graining and multiscale modeling; and [[mechanical metamaterials]].  The biological systems include flocks, evolving populations, epidemics, trees, proteins, nucleic acids, and protein/nucleic acid complexes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Condensed Matter Theory & Statistical Mechanics {{!}} Institute for Fundamental Science|author=Jane Gary |url=https://ifs.uoregon.edu/condensed-matter-theory/ |access-date=2022-04-02 |website=ifs.uoregon.edu}}</ref> }}

Belitz served as department head of physics from 1998–2004, associate dean for natural sciences from 2004–2010, and as  director of the Institute of Theoretical Science at the University of Oregon from 2013–2019.<ref name=":1" /> 

From 2005 to 2020, Belitz served as associate editor for [[Condensed matter physics|condensed matter theory]] for ''[[Reviews of Modern Physics]].''<ref name=":0" />
